Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
The snapshot looks like a period with a strong dollar (+2.0), a low unemployment rate (-1.5), and a very flat or inverted curve (spread z -2.0). Core CPI is high relative to its 3-year average, while headline CPI is near its average. The 10-year yield is low relative to its 3-year history, and gold is weak.

Candidate: early 2007 to 2008 is ruled out because the 36-month window would imply different dynamics. A better fit is 2025-2026, but the dollar was weakening in 2025, so that fits poorly.

Another candidate is 2015-2016. The unemployment rate was low relative to its own 3-year average, since it had been falling, which fits. The dollar was strong after the 2014-15 surge. Gold was down sharply over 12 months, which fits late 2014 to 2015. The 10-year yield was low, but the policy rate z of 0 with a +0.5 12-month change points to late 2015 or early 2016. Core CPI at +1.5 is odd for that period, though.

Another candidate is late 2024 to early 2025. The dollar was strong, but gold was rising then, so that fails.

Gold at -2.0 over 6 months and -2.0 over 12 months suggests a decline such as 2013 or 2014-15. Core CPI z of +1.5 against a headline z of 0 suggests energy prices were falling, which fits 2015 or early 2016. The 10-year yield z of -2.0 with a 12-month change of -1.0 fits 2016. IG credit at +1.5 over 1 month fits a rally. Payrolls z at 0 with a falling trend fits 2016. Baa spread +1.0 fits the energy-driven widening in 2015-16. The policy rate +0.5 12-month change fits after the December 2015 hike.

The 10-year yield was lowest in mid-2016, but gold rallied in early 2016, so that doesn't fit. Gold at -2.0 over 6 months fits December 2015 most closely, though the 10y-2y spread z of -2.0 is odd. The 3-year-ago spread was wide, which could explain it. I'll pick around November 2015 to January 2016, with a 6-month drawdown in equities.

Estimate: December 2015 (month-end), consistent with the Fed hike, gold bottoming, and IG credit rallying. Equity 1m return around 0 fits December 2015 (roughly -1.6%).
